the sacculus of the Gram-negative bacterium E. coli is a bag-like structure that is made of peptidoglycerol strands, which are oriented parallel to the cell membrane and encircle the cell in a single, disordered, layer.

the structural organization of the peptiglycan, the main structural component of the bacterial envelope.
the molecular architecture and function of the bacterial peptidogycan (PG) layer, the major component of the bacterial outer membrane (OM).
